'''Invasion percolation''' is a mathematical model of realistic [[Fluid simulation|fluid distributions]] for slow immiscible fluid invasion in porous media,  in [[percolation theory]].
It "explicitly takes into account the transport process taking place". A wetting fluid such as water takes over from a non-wetting fluid such as oil, and capillary forces are taken into account. It was introduced by Wilkinson and Willemsen (1983).<ref>David Wilkinson and Jorge F Willemsen, "[http://www.physics.purdue.edu/flow/MMproject/Wilkinson1983.pdf Invasion percolation: a new form of percolation theory]", ''J. Phys. A: Math. Gen.'' 16 (1983) 3365–3376.</ref>

Invasion percolation proceeds in [[avalanche]]s or bursts, and thus exhibits a form of [[intermittency]]. This avalanche behavior has been likened to [[self-organized criticality]].<ref>{{citation
 | last1 = Grassberger | first1 = P. | author1-link = Peter Grassberger
 | last2 = Manna | first2 = S. S.
 | doi = 10.1051/jphys:0199000510110107700

 }}</ref><ref>D. Sornette, A. Johansen, I. Dornic, J. Phys. I (France) 5, 325 (1995)</ref>
